issues.description: HAS_TIME regex is an under-audited heuristic with no stated invariant or measurement
issues.detail: The guard `/\dm?s/i` is a pre-filter whose correctness rests on an unstated claim: 'every value that valueParser would flag as a sub-threshold time contains a digit followed by optional m and an s.' That holds for `10ms`, `1s`, `.5s`? No — `.5s` has no digit-then-s adjacency only if you read `5s`; fine. But `1e2ms` (scientific) or values split across var() expansions would be missed. State the invariant in a comment.

issues.description: Performance claim has no measurement attached
issues.detail: The PR title is 'Fix performance' but the diff contains no benchmark, no profile, no before/after numbers — only a regex short-circuit. The optimization may well be in the critical 3%, since walkDecls runs on every declaration and valueParser is non-trivial, but the rule is measure first. Attach a microbenchmark or cite the profile from issue #6869 so reviewers can confirm this is the hot spot, not a guess.

issues.description: Regex case-insensitivity flag is redundant given downstream lowercasing but worth a literate comment
issues.detail: `decl.prop` is later lowercased, but `decl.value` is matched raw, so the `/i` flag is load-bearing for values like `10MS` or `1S`. That is fine, but a one-line comment above the regex stating 'pre-filter: skip declarations whose value contains no time-like token; case-insensitive because values are not normalized here' would make the reader's job trivial. Right now the reader has to reconstruct the reasoning.

issues.description: Regex matches inside identifiers and strings, which is harmless but worth acknowledging
issues.detail: `HAS_TIME` will match inside `url('foo1ms.png')` or a custom-ident containing `1ms`. The downstream valueParser walk will correctly ignore non-time nodes, so the pre-filter only over-accepts (false positive on the guard, never false negative on the rule). Worth noting in a comment that the regex is a fast over-approximation and exactness is delegated to valueParser — that is the literate-programming honest move.

review.summary: Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED. The change is a sensible fast-path pre-filter — short-circuit walkDecls when the value contains no time-like token — and the algorithmic shape is right: cheap regex test before expensive valueParser construction. But the PR ships three unstated claims: (1) the regex is a sound over-approximation of 'contains a time value,' (2) the bypassed work is actually the hot spot, and (3) no benchmark is attached to verify either. Add a literate comment naming the invariant ('fast over-approximation; exactness delegated to valueParser') and cite or attach the profile from #6869. The code is likely correct and likely faster, but as written it is tried, not proved.
